brief:
Israel's opposition bloc, anchored by former military chief Benny Eisenkot, faces mounting pressure to maintain cohesion across ideological lines as it attempts to convert parliamentary opposition into a governing alternative, Al Jazeera English reported. The alliance brings together parties with divergent positions on settlement expansion, Palestinian statehood, and security doctrine—divisions that have historically fractured Israeli center-left coalitions.

Eisenkot's efforts to forge a stable bloc depend on securing commitments from coalition partners on contentious issues before any potential rotation agreement or new elections. The fragility of such alliances has repeatedly complicated efforts to unseat Netanyahu, whose government has remained in office despite persistent opposition.
dek: Eisenkot's fragile alliance must overcome deep ideological divisions to turn its opposition into a government.
title: Opposition seeks unity to challenge Netanyahu's government
